CPR DLA 19: Solute Handling.prompt: CPR 2 Solute Handling how is bicarb reabsorbed in the kidney? [___]
CPR DLA 19: Solute Handling.answer: CPR 2 Solute Handling how is bicarb reabsorbed in the kidney? early proximal tubule - Na+/H+ antiporter, bicarb converted to CO2 in lumen, moves into cell, turns back into bicarb in cell, leaves into blood via channel protein. carbonic anhydrase found both in lumen and inside epithelial cells The PT secretes equal H+ for each HCO3− . Carbonic anhydrase (CA) converts the H2CO3 to CO2 and H2O. Both molecules are then recovered by simple diffusion. In the DST, the low intracellular Na+ concentration, also drives the Na/H+ antiport causing H+ secretion and bicarbonate absorption.

CPR DLA 19: Solute Handling.prompt: CPR 2 Solute Handling how is Ca++ regulated by PTH? [___]
CPR DLA 19: Solute Handling.answer: CPR 2 Solute Handling how is Ca++ regulated by PTH? low Ca++ levels causes increased PTH secretion -> decreased phosphate reabsorption, increased Ca++ reabsorption -> increase plasma Ca++ levels back to normal

CPR DLA 19: Solute Handling.prompt: CPR 2 Solute Handling what do carbonic anhydrase inhibitors do? [___]
CPR DLA 19: Solute Handling.answer: CPR 2 Solute Handling what do carbonic anhydrase inhibitors do? prevent carbonic anhydrase -> HCO3- can't be reabsorbed in proximal tubule -> HCO3- stays in urine and gets excreted -> prevents alkalosis (use acetazolamide to prevent altitude sickness). however, C.A. inhibitor also causes Na+ to stay in urine; mild diuretic (because there are plenty of opportunities in distal nephron to reabsorb Na+)

CPR DLA 19: Solute Handling.prompt: CPR 2 Solute Handling how do loop diuretics affect Ca++ reabsorption? [___]
CPR DLA 19: Solute Handling.answer: CPR 2 Solute Handling how do loop diuretics affect Ca++ reabsorption? loop diuretics inhibit Na+/K+/Cl- cotransporter -> loss of lumen positive potential -> less reabsorption of Ca++

CPR DLA 19: Solute Handling.prompt: CPR 2 Solute Handling what effect do loop diuretics have on Mg++ reabsorption? [___]
CPR DLA 19: Solute Handling.answer: CPR 2 Solute Handling what effect do loop diuretics have on Mg++ reabsorption? loop diuretics inhibit Na+/K+/Cl- triple cotransporter in thick ascending limb -> Lack of K+ means that it cannot no diffusion back into the lumen via a luminal membrane protein. This results in the loss of positive lumen potential which normally promotes Na+,Ca++, and Mg++ reabsorption via paracelllular pathway. -> Mg++ will not be reabsorbed as well -> hypomagnesemia

CPR DLA 19: Solute Handling.prompt: CPR 2 Solute Handling how is vitamin D3 regulated by Ca++ and by PTH? [___]
CPR DLA 19: Solute Handling.answer: CPR 2 Solute Handling how is vitamin D3 regulated by Ca++ and by PTH? low Ca++ increases activity of 1alpha-hydroxylase enzyme -> conversion of D3 to active form PTH increases activity of 1alpha-hydroxylase

CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.lecture: CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of the Heart
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.prompt: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart [___] are the most common form of congenital heart diseases (~25%) . They are caused by a failure of the fusion of the endocardial cushions with the primordial IV septum and the bulbar septum ; can also have an associated AV valve (usually mitral) abnormality. Patients with Down's Syndrome have a higher risk L → R shunting of blood
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.answer: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart Membranous Ventricular Septal Defects are the most common form of congenital heart diseases (~25%) . They are caused by a failure of the fusion of the endocardial cushions with the primordial IV septum and the bulbar septum ; can also have an associated AV valve (usually mitral) abnormality. Patients with Down's Syndrome have a higher risk L → R shunting of blood

CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.lecture: CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of the Heart
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.prompt: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart [___] is caused by faulty migration of [___] cells, leading to the absence of the spiral-twist in the aortico-pulmonary septum. This defect results in the switching of the aorta and pulmonary trunk , which is immediately lethal unless combined with another defect such as PDA, ASD, or VSD. [___] shunt
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.answer: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart Transposition of the Great Vessels is caused by faulty migration of neural crest cells, leading to the absence of the spiral-twist in the aortico-pulmonary septum. This defect results in the switching of the aorta and pulmonary trunk , which is immediately lethal unless combined with another defect such as PDA, ASD, or VSD. R → L shunt

CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.lecture: CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of the Heart
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.prompt: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart [___] is associated with VSDs and is caused by a failure in neural crest cell migration , leading to a failure of the formation of the aorticopulmonary septum [___] shunt
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.answer: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart Persistent Truncus Arteriosus is associated with VSDs and is caused by a failure in neural crest cell migration , leading to a failure of the formation of the aorticopulmonary septum R → L shunt

CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.lecture: CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of the Heart
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.prompt: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart [___] (reversal shunt) is a large VSD, PDA, and AVSD that quickly lead to excess volume through the right heart and pulmonary circuit causing progressive damage to the pulmonary vasculature and development of pulmonary hypertension. The pressure in the pulmonary crcuit may exceed the systemic pressure causing reversal of blood flow from the right side of circulation to the left. Results in [___] due to deoxygenated blood from the right now flowing through the systemic circulation.
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.answer: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart Eisenmenger’s syndrome (reversal shunt) is a large VSD, PDA, and AVSD that quickly lead to excess volume through the right heart and pulmonary circuit causing progressive damage to the pulmonary vasculature and development of pulmonary hypertension. The pressure in the pulmonary crcuit may exceed the systemic pressure causing reversal of blood flow from the right side of circulation to the left. Results in late cynosis due to deoxygenated blood from the right now flowing through the systemic circulation.

CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.lecture: CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of the Heart
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.prompt: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart [___] is the result of the heart in an abnormal location. [___] results from faulty development of the sternum and pericardium because of failure of complete fusion of the lateral folds during the 4th week. Death occurs in most cases during the first few days after birth, usually from infection, cardiac failure, or hypoxemia.
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.answer: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart Ectopia Cordis is the result of the heart in an abnormal location. Thoracic ectopia cordia results from faulty development of the sternum and pericardium because of failure of complete fusion of the lateral folds during the 4th week. Death occurs in most cases during the first few days after birth, usually from infection, cardiac failure, or hypoxemia.

CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.lecture: CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of the Heart
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.prompt: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart [___] result in excess volume of flow through the right heart and pulmonary circuit, resulting in inceased pressures in the pulmonary vessels. The workload of the right ventricle is increased (can lead to heart failure) and if pulmonary vascular pressures rise enough, pulmonary edema results; occurs in VSDs and PDAs
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.answer: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart L → R shunts result in excess volume of flow through the right heart and pulmonary circuit, resulting in inceased pressures in the pulmonary vessels. The workload of the right ventricle is increased (can lead to heart failure) and if pulmonary vascular pressures rise enough, pulmonary edema results; occurs in VSDs and PDAs

CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.lecture: CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of the Heart
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.prompt: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart [___] is caused by a [___] migration failure, leading to abnormal drainage of the pulmonary veins into the systemic venous circulation, resulting in severe cyanosis immediately after birth; is immediately lethal unless combined with an ASD or PDA. Common sites include the SVC , brachiocephalic vein , coronary sinus , and portal / hepatic vein R → L shunt
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.answer: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart Total Anamalous Pulmonary Venous Return (TAPVR) is caused by a neural crest cell migration failure, leading to abnormal drainage of the pulmonary veins into the systemic venous circulation, resulting in severe cyanosis immediately after birth; is immediately lethal unless combined with an ASD or PDA. Common sites include the SVC , brachiocephalic vein , coronary sinus , and portal / hepatic vein R → L shunt

CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.lecture: CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of the Heart
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.prompt: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart Down's syndrome is associated with [___] defects resulting in [___] as well as [___]
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.answer: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart Down's syndrome is associated with endocardial cushion defects resulting in ASD/VSD as well as patent ductus arteriosus (PDA)

CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.lecture: CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of the Heart
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.prompt: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart [___] is the congenital narrowing of a segment of aorta most frequent at the arch of the aorta. Incidence: male >female (2:1) and presents in 15-20% of turner syndrome patients. Can be location at different sites: preductal, postductal, and directly opposite the ductus arteriosus. Causes the development of [___] during fetal life.
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.answer: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart Coarctation of the Aorta (CoA) is the congenital narrowing of a segment of aorta most frequent at the arch of the aorta. Incidence: male >female (2:1) and presents in 15-20% of turner syndrome patients. Can be location at different sites: preductal, postductal, and directly opposite the ductus arteriosus. Causes the development of collateral circulation during fetal life.

CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.lecture: CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of the Heart
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.prompt: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart [___] can occur if the right 4th aortic arch and the proximal part of the right dorsal aorta are obliterated. The anomalous artery crosses the midline behind the esophagus and could compress it.
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.answer: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart Anomalous right subclavian artery can occur if the right 4th aortic arch and the proximal part of the right dorsal aorta are obliterated. The anomalous artery crosses the midline behind the esophagus and could compress it.

CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.lecture: CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of the Heart
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.prompt: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart Turner syndrome is associated with [___] of the aorta
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.answer: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart Turner syndrome is associated with coarctation of the aorta

CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.lecture: CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of the Heart
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.prompt: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart [___] results from the ductus arteriosus failing to close, and results in a L → R shunt. Clincally associated with Down's syndrome
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.answer: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart Patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) results from the ductus arteriosus failing to close, and results in a L → R shunt. Clincally associated with Down's syndrome

CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.lecture: CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of the Heart
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.prompt: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart [___] shunts result in venous blood from the right heart (pulmonary circuit) mixing with the arterial blood of the left heart. Because of this, there is decreased pulmonary blood flow, leading to cyanosis . They are primarily caused by ASDs or VSDs associated with high pressure on the right side of the heart; can be caused by congenital defects, tricuspid atresia, and total anamolous pulmonary connection
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.answer: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart Right → Left shunts result in venous blood from the right heart (pulmonary circuit) mixing with the arterial blood of the left heart. Because of this, there is decreased pulmonary blood flow, leading to cyanosis . They are primarily caused by ASDs or VSDs associated with high pressure on the right side of the heart; can be caused by congenital defects, tricuspid atresia, and total anamolous pulmonary connection

CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.lecture: CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of the Heart
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.prompt: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart [___] type atrial septal defects are a form of endocardial cushion defects which are caused by the foramen primum failing to close; often present in Down's Syndrome
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.answer: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart Primum type atrial septal defects are a form of endocardial cushion defects which are caused by the foramen primum failing to close; often present in Down's Syndrome

CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.lecture: CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of the Heart
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.prompt: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart Infections such as rubella in early pregnancy is associated with increased risk for [___]
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.answer: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart Infections such as rubella in early pregnancy is associated with increased risk for patent ductus arteriosus (PDA)

CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.lecture: CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of the Heart
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.prompt: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart [___] occurs if there is a persistence of the entire right dorsal aorta and abnormal involution of the distal part of the left dorsal aorta. Two types: -Without retroesophageal component -With a retroesophageal component
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.answer: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart Right aortic arch occurs if there is a persistence of the entire right dorsal aorta and abnormal involution of the distal part of the left dorsal aorta. Two types: -Without retroesophageal component -With a retroesophageal component

CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.lecture: CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of the Heart
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.prompt: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart [___] can occur if the right dosal aorta between the origin of the 7th intersegmental artery and its junction with the left dorsal aorta fails to disappear. Resulting in a vascular ring surrounding the trachea and esophagus, compressing them and causing problems with breathing and swallowing.
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.answer: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart Double aortic arch can occur if the right dosal aorta between the origin of the 7th intersegmental artery and its junction with the left dorsal aorta fails to disappear. Resulting in a vascular ring surrounding the trachea and esophagus, compressing them and causing problems with breathing and swallowing.

CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.lecture: CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of the Heart
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.prompt: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart [___] is caused by the absence of the interatrial septum, resulting in 1 atrium and 2 ventricles
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.answer: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart Common atrium (cor trilovulare biventriculare) is caused by the absence of the interatrial septum, resulting in 1 atrium and 2 ventricles

CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.lecture: CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of the Heart
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.prompt: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart Sinus venosus type atrial septal defects are caused by defective absorption of sinus venosus into the [___]
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.answer: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart Sinus venosus type atrial septal defects are caused by defective absorption of sinus venosus into the right atrium

CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.lecture: CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of the Heart
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.prompt: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart [___] is the most common atrial septal defect, and is caused by a failure in the fusion between the septum primum and secundum
CPR Lecture 6: Clinical Embryology of th.answer: CPR 1 Clinical Embryology of the Heart Patent foramen ovale is the most common atrial septal defect, and is caused by a failure in the fusion between the septum primum and secundum
